verdict_reason: Tab lookup is correct and fully tested, but the tab copy is keyed by a camelCase alias (copyKey) while every other address-type copy is keyed by the ADDRESS_TYPES value.

todos.issue: One concept, two key schemes: the address type keys its copy by its ADDRESS_TYPES value in copy.addressType.options (copy.en.js:91-101) and copy.roles.legendByAddressType (copy.en.js:108-112), but by a camelCase alias in copy.list.tabs (copy.en.js:24-37: originOrConsignor, destinationConsigneeOrImporter, branch; same in copy.cy.js:26-39). The alias forces a second name on every tab, tabFor(addressType, copyKey) at address-book-tabs.js:6-20, which list.controller.js:67 and :173 read instead of the address type.
todos.fix: Must: each address type's copy is keyed by its ADDRESS_TYPES value everywhere in copy.en.js and copy.cy.js, and a tab finds its label and heading by its addressType, with no separate copyKey. One way: rename copy.list.tabs keys to ORIGIN_OR_CONSIGNOR, DESTINATION_CONSIGNEE_OR_IMPORTER and BRANCH in both bundles, drop copyKey from tabFor, read copy.list.tabs[tab.addressType] in list.controller.js, and update copy.test.js, list.tabs.controller.test.js and add.fit.spec.js.
